cards.explanation: The answer is an eternal house in heaven. Paul says that if the earthly tent is dismantled, "…we have a building from God, an eternal house in heaven, not built by human hands." (2 Corinthians 5:1) A tent is a temporary place to stay, friends, and this house is the opposite. It comes from God, and it doesn't pack up.

The answer is False. Paul says the house is "…a building from God, an eternal house in heaven, not built by human hands." (2 Corinthians 5:1) The house comes from God, not from human builders. That's why this one is False, friends.

The answer is to be clothed with our heavenly dwelling. Paul says, "…in this tent we groan, longing to be clothed with our heavenly dwelling…" (2 Corinthians 5:2) The groaning isn't random, bakers. It points toward something we're longing for. Paul pictures that dwelling as something we put on, like clothes.

The answer is naked. Paul says, "…when we are clothed, we will not be found naked." (2 Corinthians 5:3) He's using the picture of clothing for the heavenly dwelling, friends. Once we're clothed, we won't be found without it.

The answer is True. Paul says, "…we groan under our burdens, because we do not wish to be unclothed but clothed…" (2 Corinthians 5:4) The wish is to be clothed, bakers, and the burdens are why he's groaning.

The answer is life. Paul says we wish to be clothed "…so that our mortality may be swallowed up by life." (2 Corinthians 5:4) Notice what's doing the swallowing, friends. It's life, and mortality is what gets swallowed.

The answer is the Spirit. Paul says God "…has given us the Spirit as a pledge of what is to come." (2 Corinthians 5:5) A pledge is a promise you can hold onto, bakers. So the Spirit is how God backs up what's coming.

The answer is True. Paul says, "…we are always confident, although we know that while we are at home in the body, we are away from the Lord." (2 Corinthians 5:6) Both things are true at once, friends. Away from the Lord for now, and still confident.
The answer is by faith and not by sight. Paul says, "…we walk by faith, not by sight." (2 Corinthians 5:7) Faith is how we walk, bakers, and sight is not.

The word is prefer. Paul says, "We are confident, then, and would prefer to be away from the body and at home with the Lord." (2 Corinthians 5:8) Being at home with the Lord is what he'd choose, friends.

The answer is to please the Lord. Paul says, "…we aspire to please Him, whether we are at home in this body or away from it." (2 Corinthians 5:9) The aim doesn't change with the address, bakers. At home in the body or away from it, the goal stays the same.

The answer is before the judgment seat of Christ. Paul says, "…we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ…" (2 Corinthians 5:10) Notice the word "all," friends. It includes every one of us, Paul too.

The answer is False. Paul says we appear "…that each one may receive his due for the things done in the body, whether good or bad." (2 Corinthians 5:10) Both good and bad are named, so "only the good" doesn't match the text. Notice he says "each one," bakers, so nobody is left out.
